files.title: How to use this kit
files.body:
# Node agent kit — Operate

A ready project folder for running this act with your agent. People drive, decide and sign off; agents help.

## What's inside
- **Context file** — `AGENTS.md`: What the agent always knows about the initiative: how we work, the lifecycle, conventions, trace IDs, templates, ground rules and scale.
- **Skills** — `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: Reusable how-to packages — one per technique or method — with steps, structure, output templates and checks. The agent loads one when the task needs it.
- **Commands** — `commands/<name>.md`: Saved prompts you run by name, with arguments — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act.
- **Workflows** — `workflows/<name>.md`: A run specification: steps in order, inputs and outputs as files, who owns each step, human checkpoints, decision branches, recovery and the gate.
- **Subagents** — `agents/<name>.md`: Specialised helpers with one job — lens reviewers (privacy, security, finance…), a researcher, a synthesiser, a challenger, a decision-brief writer.
- **Tools & connectors** — `TOOLS.md`: Which tools and data each step needs — web search, documents, spreadsheets, the backlog tool, the research repository, the code repository — and what each scale allows the agent to do with them.
- **Guardrails & hooks** — `GUARDRAILS.md`: Rules the agent must follow and automatic checks at key moments — before saving an artifact, before a decision, before sending anything outside the team.
- **Rubrics** — `rubrics/<artifact>.md`: A scored checklist for each artifact, from its template, quality criteria and the unit's criteria.
- **Memory & handoff** — `PROGRESS.md · TRACE.md · docs/`: What carries across sessions and people: the project folder, a progress log, and a trace-ID register.
- **Templates** — `templates/`: the artifact templates the work produces.

## Set it up
1. Put this folder at the root of your project repository or shared drive and fill `{{initiative}}` in AGENTS.md.
2. Point your agent at it — how each layer is picked up:
   - Context file: Many coding agents read AGENTS.md at the repository root. Tools with their own file (e.g. CLAUDE.md) can import or copy it. In chat assistants, paste it into the project's instructions.
   - Skills: Agents that support skills load SKILL.md folders from their skills directory. Otherwise attach the SKILL.md as a file, or paste it before the prompt.
   - Commands: Agents with custom commands or saved prompts read Markdown files from their commands / prompts folder; $ARGUMENTS takes what you type after the name. Otherwise paste the file.
   - Workflows: Point the agent at the workflow file ("run workflows/x.md, stop at every checkpoint"). Orchestration tools can execute the YAML block; people can read it as a checklist.
   - Subagents: Agents that support subagents load them from their agents folder. Otherwise open a separate conversation and paste the file as its first message.
   - Tools & connectors: Connect tools through your agent's connectors or MCP servers; grant the least access the step needs.
   - Guardrails & hooks: Agents with hooks can run these checks automatically; everywhere else they're a checklist the agent applies and you confirm.
   - Rubrics: Any agent: "score docs/x.md against rubrics/x.md".
   - Memory & handoff: Keep them in the repository or shared drive the agent can read; start each session with "read PROGRESS.md".
3. Start with the command `operate-run-act`, or the command for the unit you're on.
4. After every step: check the output, score it against its rubric, save it in `docs/`, and log it in PROGRESS.md.

Tools change quickly — check your agent's documentation for where it reads context files, skills, commands and subagents.

# Burn-rate calculation

_Technique_ — How fast an error budget is being spent relative to spending it exactly over the window.

## When to use it
SLO alerts and budget reports.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.1.1.1 S3 Set targets from baselines — command `operate-7-1-1-1-s3-set-targets-from-baselines`
- 7.1.3.1 S1 Derive burn-rate thresholds — command `operate-7-1-3-1-s1-derive-burn-rate-thresholds`
- 7.1.4.1 S1 Compute budget consumption — command `operate-7-1-4-1-s1-compute-budget-consumption`

## How to do it
1. Burn rate = observed error rate ÷ (1 − SLO)
2. Budget spent in time t = burn rate × t ÷ window

## Structure
- **Observed bad rate:** e.g. 8%
- **Allowed (1 − SLO):** 5%
- **Burn rate:** 1.6×
- **Window:** 28 days

# Error budget

_Pattern_ — The amount of unreliability an SLO allows (1 − target) over its window, spent deliberately on change and protected by a policy agreed in advance.

Every SLO.

---

# ITIL 4

_Framework_ — AXELOS's framework for IT service management. Its service value system links demand to value through governance, practices and continual improvement, and covers services from design to retirement.

## When to use it
Continual improvement of running services, service portfolio decisions and service retirement.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.2.1.1 S4 Declare & log the incident (applied as: incident management) — command `operate-7-2-1-1-s3-declare-and-log-the-incident`
- 7.2.2.1 S2 Set severity from the matrix (applied as: incident management) — command `operate-7-2-2-1-s2-set-severity-from-the-matrix`
- 7.2.2.2 S5 Brief service desk, sponsor & ops manager (applied as: incident management) — command `operate-7-2-2-2-s4-brief-service-desk-sponsor-and-ops-manager`
- 7.2.3.1 S4 Put affected data right (applied as: incident management) — command `operate-7-2-3-1-s3-put-affected-data-right`
- 7.3.1.1 S3 New problem? (applied as: problem management) — command `operate-7-3-1-1-d1-new-problem`
- 7.3.2.1 S4 Cause proven? (applied as: problem management) — command `operate-7-3-2-1-d1-cause-proven`
- 7.3.3.1 S3 Safe and effective? (applied as: problem management) — command `operate-7-3-3-1-d1-safe-and-effective`
- 7.3.4.1 S4 Fix now? (applied as: problem management) — command `operate-7-3-4-1-d1-fix-now`
- 7.4.1.1 S3 Define tiers & escalations (applied as: service desk) — command `operate-7-4-1-1-s3-define-tiers-and-escalations`
- 7.4.2.1 S3 Fulfil by the request model (applied as: service request management) — command `operate-7-4-2-1-s2-fulfil-by-the-request-model`
- 7.4.3.1 S4 Route with the decision recorded (applied as: service desk) — command `operate-7-4-3-1-s3-route-with-the-decision-recorded`
- 7.5.1.1 S4 Business owner agrees? (applied as: capacity and performance management) — command `operate-7-5-1-1-d1-business-owner-agrees`
- 7.5.2.1 S4 Scale, tune or raise quotas (applied as: capacity and performance management) — command `operate-7-5-2-1-s3-scale-tune-or-raise-quotas`

## How to do it
1. Start from the value the service co-creates with its consumers
2. Run the service value chain: plan, improve, engage, design & transition, obtain / build, deliver & support
3. Apply the continual improvement model to every service
4. Retire services deliberately through service configuration and portfolio management

## Structure
1. **What is the vision?** — Business goals
2. **Where are we now?** — Baseline assessment
3. **Where do we want to be?** — Measurable targets
4. **How do we get there?** — Improvement plan
5. **Take action** — Execute the plan
6. **Did we get there?** — Measurements and KPIs
7. **How do we keep the momentum going?** — Embed and repeat
→ then repeat

## Output

- Incident record → `templates/incident-record.md`, saved as `docs/incident-record.md`
- Stakeholder update → `templates/incident-update.md`, saved as `docs/incident-update.md`

- Avoid: Improvement registers no one prioritises

- Support model: Every tier staffed

- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

# Multi-level backlog

_Pattern_ — Keeps work in linked backlogs at different sizes and horizons — initiatives, epics and features, stories — each owned and refined at its own cadence, so strategy traces down to the sprint and evidence traces back up.

## When to use it
Any organisation running more than one team or initiative.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.3.4.1 S3 Rank against features — command `operate-7-3-4-1-s3-rank-against-features`

## How to do it
1. Portfolio backlog: initiatives, ranked quarterly by the portfolio board
2. Product backlog: epics and features, ordered by the product owner
3. Iteration backlog: stories pulled into a sprint by the team
4. Link every item to its parent
5. Detail just in time — the further out, the coarser

## Structure
- **Portfolio backlog** — Initiatives · quarters · portfolio board
  - **Product backlog** — Epics → features · months · product owner
    - **Iteration backlog** — Stories → tasks · one sprint · delivery team

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Product backlog entry → `templates/product-backlog.md`, saved as `docs/product-backlog.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: One giant backlog mixing initiatives and tasks
- Avoid: Stories with no parent — work nobody can trace to an outcome
- Avoid: Detailing everything up front
- Product backlog entry: Every item traces to an initiative, problem or improvement
- Product backlog entry: Ordered — no two items share a rank
- Product backlog entry: Only the next 1–2 quarters detailed
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

---
name: multi-window-burn-rate-alerting
description: "Alerts on how fast an error budget is being spent, using a long window for significance and a short window to reset quickly, at several burn rates. Use when every SLO with enough traffic. In Node: 7.1.3.1 S1 Derive burn-rate thresholds."
---

# Multi-window burn-rate alerting

_Pattern_ — Alerts on how fast an error budget is being spent, using a long window for significance and a short window to reset quickly, at several burn rates.

## When to use it
Every SLO with enough traffic.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.1.3.1 S1 Derive burn-rate thresholds — command `operate-7-1-3-1-s1-derive-burn-rate-thresholds`

## How to do it
1. Pick the share of budget worth waking someone for (e.g. 2% in 1 h)
2. Convert to a burn rate (2% of 28 days in 1 h ≈ 14.4×)
3. Require both the long window (1 h) and a short window (5 min) to exceed it
4. Add a slower page (6× over 6 h) and a ticket (1× over 3 days)

## Structure
| Severity | Burn rate | Long window | Short window | Budget spent |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Page | 14.4× | 1 h | 5 min | 2% |
| Page | 6× | 6 h | 30 min | 5% |
| Ticket | 1× | 3 days | 6 h | 10% |

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Burn-rate alert rules → `templates/alert-rules.md`, saved as `docs/alert-rules.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Threshold alerts on raw error rates
- Avoid: One window only — slow to reset
- Burn-rate alert rules: Every alert actionable
- Burn-rate alert rules: Every alert has a runbook step
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
Google SRE Workbook, 'Alerting on SLOs'

In Node: 7.6.1.1 S1 Match findings to the SBOM; 7.6.2.1 S1 Map threats to use cases; 7.6.3.1 S4 Eradicate & recover; 7.6.4.1 S5 Report posture with evidence."
---

# NIST Cybersecurity Framework

_Framework_ — NIST's framework (CSF 2.0) organising cybersecurity outcomes into six functions: Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover.

## When to use it
Organising security operations so nothing falls between the functions.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.6.1.1 S1 Match findings to the SBOM (applied as: identify and protect) — command `operate-7-6-1-1-s1-match-findings-to-the-sbom`
- 7.6.2.1 S1 Map threats to use cases (applied as: detect) — command `operate-7-6-2-1-s1-map-threats-to-use-cases`
- 7.6.3.1 S4 Eradicate & recover (applied as: respond and recover) — command `operate-7-6-3-1-s3-eradicate-and-recover`
- 7.6.4.1 S5 Report posture with evidence (applied as: protect) — command `operate-7-6-4-1-s4-report-posture-with-evidence`

## How to do it
1. Govern — set strategy, roles and policy
2. Identify — know assets, risks and weaknesses
3. Protect — safeguards such as access control and patching
4. Detect — find attacks and anomalies
5. Respond — contain and act on incidents
6. Recover — restore and improve

## Structure
1. **Govern** — Roles, policy, risk strategy
2. **Identify** — Assets, SBOM, vulnerabilities
3. **Protect** — Access, patching, secrets
4. **Detect** — Monitoring and detections
5. **Respond** — Containment, notification
6. **Recover** — Restore and learn
→ then repeat

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Scanner findings → `templates/vulnerability-register.md`, saved as `docs/vulnerability-register.md`
- Detection rule catalogue → `templates/detection-catalogue.md`, saved as `docs/detection-catalogue.md`
- Incident timeline → `templates/incident-timeline.md`, saved as `docs/incident-timeline.md`
- Security posture report → `templates/posture-report.md`, saved as `docs/posture-report.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Treating it as a compliance checklist
- Scanner findings: Exposure and exploitability, not CVSS alone
- Scanner findings: SLA and owner per item
- Detection rule catalogue: Each high threat covered
- Detection rule catalogue: Tested monthly
- Incident timeline: Every action timestamped
- Incident timeline: Sources linked
- Security posture report: Evidence linked
- Security posture report: Actions owned
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
NIST Cybersecurity Framework 2.0 (2024)

files.body:
---
name: site-reliability-engineering
description: "Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away. Use when any service people depend on — scaled down for small teams, never skipped. In Node: 7.1.1.1 S2 Choose SLIs per journey; 7.1.2.1 S4 Dashboard matches raw events?; 7.1.3.1 S1 Derive burn-rate thresholds; 7.1.4.1 S3 Budget left in every SLO?; 7.2.3.1 S3 SLIs recovered?; 7.2.4.1 S4 Blameless, evidenced, actions owned?."
---

# Site Reliability Engineering

_Framework_ — Google's discipline of running services with software-engineering methods: reliability is defined by SLOs, the gap to 100% is an error budget to spend on change, and toil is engineered away.

## When to use it
Any service people depend on — scaled down for small teams, never skipped.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.1.1.1 S2 Choose SLIs per journey (applied as: SLIs and SLOs) — command `operate-7-1-1-1-s2-choose-slis-per-journey`
- 7.1.2.1 S4 Dashboard matches raw events? (applied as: monitoring) — command `operate-7-1-2-1-d1-dashboard-matches-raw-events`
- 7.1.3.1 S1 Derive burn-rate thresholds (applied as: alerting on SLOs) — command `operate-7-1-3-1-s1-derive-burn-rate-thresholds`
- 7.1.4.1 S3 Budget left in every SLO? (applied as: error budget policy) — command `operate-7-1-4-1-d1-budget-left-in-every-slo`
- 7.2.3.1 S3 SLIs recovered? (applied as: emergency response) — command `operate-7-2-3-1-d1-slis-recovered`
- 7.2.4.1 S4 Blameless, evidenced, actions owned? (applied as: postmortem culture) — command `operate-7-2-4-1-d1-blameless-evidenced-actions-owned`
- 7.5.2.1 S2 Compare with forecast & headroom policy (applied as: capacity planning) — command `operate-7-5-2-1-s2-compare-with-forecast-and-headroom-policy`

## How to do it
1. Define SLIs from what users experience
2. Set SLOs below 100% and agree an error-budget policy
3. Alert on budget burn, not on causes
4. Respond to incidents with clear command and blameless postmortems
5. Cap toil and plan capacity ahead of demand

## Structure
| Practice | What it gives you |
| --- | --- |
| SLIs & SLOs | A shared, numeric definition of 'reliable enough' |
| Error budgets | A rule for choosing between shipping and fixing |
| Monitoring & alerting | Pages only for user-visible burn |
| Emergency response & postmortems | Fast restore and learning without blame |
| Capacity planning | Demand met with headroom |
| Toil reduction | Time for engineering, not repetition |

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- SLI specification → `templates/slo-spec.md`, saved as `docs/slo-spec.md`
- Burn-rate alert rules → `templates/alert-rules.md`, saved as `docs/alert-rules.md`
- Capacity plan → `templates/capacity-plan.md`, saved as `docs/capacity-plan.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: Copying Google's tooling instead of its practices
- Avoid: SLOs set at 100%
- Avoid: An 'SRE team' that just does operations
- SLI specification: Ratio of good to valid events
- SLI specification: Target, window and owner
- SLI specification: Below 100%
- Burn-rate alert rules: Every alert actionable
- Burn-rate alert rules: Every alert has a runbook step
- Capacity plan: Range, not a point
- Capacity plan: Allocation confirmed in writing
- Capacity plan: Skills gaps named
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
Beyer et al., Site Reliability Engineering (2016) and The Site Reliability Workbook (2018)

## When to use it
you need to capture while solving

files.title: WSJF
files.body:
---
name: wsjf
description: "Weighted Shortest Job First: rank work by cost of delay divided by job size, so the most valuable small items go first. Use when ranking initiatives in the portfolio backlog and large features in the product backlog. In Node: 7.3.4.1 S3 Rank against features."
---

# WSJF

_Technique_ — Weighted Shortest Job First: rank work by cost of delay divided by job size, so the most valuable small items go first.

## When to use it
Ranking initiatives in the portfolio backlog and large features in the product backlog.

Applied in Node at:
- 7.3.4.1 S3 Rank against features — command `operate-7-3-4-1-s3-rank-against-features`

## How to do it
1. Estimate cost of delay (value + time criticality + risk reduction)
2. Estimate job size
3. Divide and rank

## Structure
> WSJF = cost of delay ÷ job size → highest first.

## Output
Write results with these templates:
- Product backlog entry → `templates/product-backlog.md`, saved as `docs/product-backlog.md`

## Quality checks
- Avoid: False precision — use relative scales
- Product backlog entry: Every item traces to an initiative, problem or improvement
- Product backlog entry: Ordered — no two items share a rank
- Product backlog entry: Only the next 1–2 quarters detailed
- Every claim cites evidence or is marked "Assumption:"

## Source
Don Reinertsen; SAFe

# Postmortem PM-118 — Faxed orders misread at Site 2

- **Incident:** 
- **Severity:** 
- **Author:** 
- **Date:** 
- **Status: Draft / Reviewed / Published:** 

## Summary
_Two or three sentences a busy reader understands._
> Example: A batch of 200-dpi faxed orders was misread; 37 orders got wrong quantities and were caught before picking. Restored in 34 minutes after declaration.


## Impact
_Users, orders, money, SLOs._
> Example: 37 orders held 2 h; 0 wrong shipments; SLO-03 budget 62% consumed.


## Timeline
_From the incident timeline._
> Example: 08:40 batch → 09:05 page → 09:12 declared → 09:31 flag → 09:46 recovered.


## Contributing factors
_How the system allowed it — no names as causes._
> Example: Fax gateway emits 200 dpi; OCR confidence over-confident below 300 dpi; one global 90% threshold; SLI not split by source, so detection took 25 min; no hold on low-confidence orders.


## What went well
_Keep doing._
> Example: Flag-per-source mitigation was in the runbook and worked first time.


## Actions
_Each owned and dated._
> Example: A1 per-source threshold (STY-140, Dev lead, 10 Oct) · A2 SLI by source (SRE, 17 Oct) · A3 warehouse hold for corrected orders (Ops manager, 14 Oct) · A4 root cause → PRB-002 (Problem manager).

# Problem investigation — PRB-002 Low-quality scans misread

- **Service:** 
- **Owner:** 
- **Version:** 
- **Status: Draft / In review / Approved:** 
- **Last updated:** 

## Problem
_What recurs, with links._
> Example: Line misreads on scanned PDFs; INC-118, INC-112; 41 contacts since 22 Sep.


## Evidence
_Samples, logs, data._
> Example: 400 anonymised pages: accuracy 98.1% at ≥ 300 dpi, 86.4% at 200 dpi.


## Hypotheses and tests
_Each candidate cause and how it was tested._
> Example: H1 fax resolution → re-scanned 50 faxes at 300 dpi: 97.9% ✔ · H2 layout drift → no change ✖.


## Root cause
_The proven cause._
> Example: OCR model trained on ≥ 300 dpi; fax gateway down-samples to 200 dpi; confidence scores over-confident on low-res digits (5↔6, 1↔7).


## Contributing causes
_What let it hurt._
> Example: Single global confidence threshold; no SLI by source.


## Fix options
_With cost and risk._
> Example: Gateway to 300 dpi (vendor config) · calibrate confidence on low-res samples · retrain.


## Sign-off

files.title: Workflow 7.1.1.1 · Set SLOs & the Budget Policy
files.body:
# Workflow 7.1.1.1 · Set SLOs & the Budget Policy

Turn the journeys users depend on into SLIs, set targets from real baselines and agree what happens when the budget runs out.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-1-1-set-slos.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-1-1-run-set-slos`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-1-1-1-set-slos
title: "Set SLOs & the Budget Policy"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/release-record.md"
  - "docs/ops-pdv.md"
  - "docs/ops-slo-targets.md"
preconditions:
  - "Service live in at least one site"
  - "28 days of data, or the SLO marked provisional"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Map critical user journeys"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s1-map-critical-user-journeys
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/critical-journeys.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Journey not worth an SLO → monitor only": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Choose SLIs per journey"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s2-choose-slis-per-journey
    skills: [site-reliability-engineering, golden-signals, red-method]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, ai-reviewer]
    output: "docs/slo-spec.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Set targets from baselines"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s3-set-targets-from-baselines
    skills: [burn-rate-calculation]
    reviewers: [performance-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/slo-spec.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Owners agree targets & budget policy?"
    owner: "Service owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Service owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Target disputed → re-derive from baseline": s3
      "Owners deadlocked → sponsor": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish SLOs & policy"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s4-publish-slos-and-policy
    skills: [error-budget]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/error-budget-policy.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "SLO Agreement"
criteria:
  - "Good / valid ratio, target, window and owner for every SLO"
checks:
  - "Baseline check"
  - "Product owner reads each SLO as user impact"
on_failure:
  - "Re-derive the SLI from user-facing events"
  - "Set a provisional SLO with a review date"
rework: "Disputed target → re-derive from the baseline"
outputs:
  - "docs/critical-journeys.md"
  - "docs/slo-spec.md"
  - "docs/error-budget-policy.md"
handoff: "SLO specification & error-budget policy → 7.1.2 Instrument & Build Dashboards"
learning:
  - "SLOs revised in their first quarter, and why — learning log"
```

files.title: Subprocess 7.1.1 · Define SLIs & SLOs
files.body:
# Subprocess 7.1.1 · Define SLIs & SLOs

Agree, in numbers, how reliable the service must be for its users — no more, no less.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-1-slis-and-slos.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-1-run-slis-and-slos`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: operate-7-1-1-slis-and-slos
title: "Define SLIs & SLOs"
owner: "SRE lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/release-record.md"
  - "docs/ops-pdv.md"
  - "docs/ops-slo-targets.md"
entry:
  - "Release record and post-deployment verification received"
  - "SLO targets from DESIGN's quality-attribute scenarios available"
runs:
  - unit: "7.1.1.1 Set SLOs & the Budget Policy"
    spec: workflows/operate-7-1-1-1-set-slos.md
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-run-set-slos
    gate: "SLO Agreement"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Journey mapping ∥ baseline pull from post-deployment verification"
gate: "SLO Agreement"
decided_by: "Service owner and product owner jointly sign the SLOs and the budget policy; the sponsor settles disputes."
criteria:
  - "Each SLI is a ratio of good events to valid events"
  - "Each SLO has a target, a window and an owner"
  - "No target at 100%"
routes:
  forward: "→ Instrument & Build Dashboards"
  rework: "Target contradicted by the data → re-derive from the baseline"
  alternate: "No baseline → provisional SLO with a review date"
  escalate: "Owners disagree on a target → sponsor"
  stop: "Journey not worth an SLO → monitor only, reason recorded — recorded in the learning log"
outputs:
  - "docs/critical-journeys.md"
  - "docs/slo-spec.md"
  - "docs/error-budget-policy.md"
handoff: "SLO specification & error-budget policy → 7.1.2 Instrument & Build Dashboards"
```

files.title: Workflow 7.1.2.1 · Instrument the Service & Build the Dashboard
files.body:
# Workflow 7.1.2.1 · Instrument the Service & Build the Dashboard

Close the telemetry gaps behind each SLI, build the dashboard and prove it shows what really happened.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-2-1-instrument.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-2-1-run-instrument`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-1-2-1-instrument
title: "Instrument the Service & Build the Dashboard"
owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/slo-spec.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
preconditions:
  - "SLOs agreed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Check telemetry against each SLI"
    owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-2-1-s1-check-telemetry-against-each-sli
    skills: [golden-signals, red-method, use-method]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/telemetry-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Gap needs code → engineering lead schedules it": authority
      "SLI unmeasurable → back to SLO definition": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Instrument the gaps"
    owner: "Developer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-2-1-s2-instrument-the-gaps
    reviewers: [privacy-reviewer, data-reviewer, engineering-reviewer]
    output: "docs/telemetry-catalogue.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Build the service dashboard"
    owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-2-1-s3-build-the-service-dashboard
    skills: [dashboards-as-code]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer, performance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/service-dashboard.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Dashboard matches raw events?"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; SRE lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Mismatch → fix instrumentation or query": s2
  - id: s4
    do: "Link the dashboard from the runbook"
    owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-2-1-s4-link-the-dashboard-from-the-runbook
    skills: [runbook]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/runbook.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Telemetry Verified"
criteria:
  - "Every SLI traced to its event source"
checks:
  - "20-event spot-check"
on_failure:
  - "Rebuild the SLI query from raw events"
  - "Redact, purge and add a log filter"
rework: "Mismatch → fix the instrumentation or the query"
outputs:
  - "docs/telemetry-catalogue.md"
  - "docs/service-dashboard.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
handoff: "Service dashboard, telemetry catalogue & updated runbook → 7.1.3 Alert on SLO Burn"
learning:
  - "Telemetry gaps found only during incidents — learning log"
```

files.title: Workflow 7.1.3.1 · Write & Test Burn-Rate Alerts
files.body:
# Workflow 7.1.3.1 · Write & Test Burn-Rate Alerts

Derive fast- and slow-burn alerts from each error budget, prove them against history and injected faults, and route them to people who know what to do.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-3-1-alerts.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-3-1-run-alerts`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-1-3-1-alerts
title: "Write & Test Burn-Rate Alerts"
owner: "SRE lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/slo-spec.md"
  - "docs/service-dashboard.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
preconditions:
  - "Dashboard verified"
  - "Rota exists or is being staffed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Derive burn-rate thresholds"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-3-1-s1-derive-burn-rate-thresholds
    skills: [multi-window-burn-rate-alerting, burn-rate-calculation, site-reliability-engineering]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, challenger]
    output: "docs/alert-rules.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Link each alert to a runbook step"
    owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-3-1-s2-link-each-alert-to-a-runbook-step
    skills: [runbook]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/runbook.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Test by replay and fault injection"
    owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-3-1-s3-test-by-replay-and-fault-injection
    skills: [fault-injection]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, reliability-reviewer]
    output: "docs/alert-test-log.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Actionable and quiet enough?"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; SRE lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Noisy or silent → re-tune thresholds": s1
      "Cause alert with no user impact → delete": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Route to the on-call rota"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-3-1-s4-route-to-the-on-call-rota
    skills: [on-call-rotation]
    reviewers: [support-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/on-call-rota.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Rota gap → service owner": authority
gate: "Alert Review"
criteria:
  - "Fast burn pages; slow burn tickets"
  - "Each alert names a runbook step"
checks:
  - "90-day replay"
  - "Fault injection in staging"
on_failure:
  - "Add a shorter window or lower threshold"
  - "Group alerts by SLO and deduplicate"
rework: "Noisy or silent in test → re-tune the thresholds"
outputs:
  - "docs/alert-rules.md"
  - "docs/alert-test-log.md"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 7.1.4.1 · Review the Error Budget

Compute how much of each error budget is spent, say what spent it, and apply the agreed policy — continue, slow down or freeze.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-4-1-budget-review.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-4-1-run-budget-review`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-1-4-1-budget-review
title: "Review the Error Budget"
owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
inputs:
  - "docs/slo-spec.md"
  - "docs/error-budget-policy.md"
  - "docs/incident-record.md"
  - "docs/deployment-record.md"
preconditions:
  - "A full 28-day window of SLI data"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Compute budget consumption"
    owner: "SRE / on-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-4-1-s1-compute-budget-consumption
    skills: [burn-rate-calculation]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer]
    output: "docs/error-budget-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Attribute burn to causes"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-4-1-s2-attribute-burn-to-causes
    skills: [change-correlation, trend-analysis]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, reliability-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/error-budget-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Budget left in every SLO?"
    owner: "Service owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Service owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Budget healthy → publish, releases continue": s4
      "Attribution disputed → re-attribute": s2
  - id: s3
    do: "Apply the policy: freeze feature releases"
    owner: "Service owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-4-1-s3-apply-the-policy-freeze-feature-releases
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, business-reviewer]
    output: "docs/release-freeze.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Freeze disputed → sponsor / CTO": authority
      "Budget spent → feature releases stop until the SLO recovers": stop
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish report & signals"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-4-1-s4-publish-report-and-signals
    skills: [operations-review]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/error-budget-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "SLO & Error Budget"
criteria:
  - "Consumption from SLI data"
  - "Every burn above 10% attributed"
checks:
  - "Recorder and judge are different people"
on_failure:
  - "Release manager blocks non-exempt changes at Go / No-Go"
  - "Re-run attribution from incident and deployment records"
rework: "Attribution disputed → re-attribute from the records"
outputs:
  - "docs/error-budget-report.md"
  - "docs/release-freeze.md"
  - "docs/signal-digest.md"
handoff: "Error-budget report & signal digest → Run the Monthly Operations Review and EVOLVE; release freeze notice → RELEASE (Go / No-Go)"
learning:
  - "Freezes, their causes and how long recovery took — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 7.1.4.2 · Run the Monthly Operations Review

Once a month, look at the whole service at once — SLOs, incidents, problems, support, capacity, cost and security — decide what needs work, and send the signals to EVOLVE.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-4-2-ops-review.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-4-2-run-ops-review`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-1-4-2-ops-review
title: "Run the Monthly Operations Review"
owner: "SRE lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/error-budget-report.md"
  - "docs/incident-record.md"
  - "docs/problem-record.md"
  - "docs/support-report.md"
  - "docs/cost-report.md"
  - "docs/posture-report.md"
preconditions:
  - "Monthly reports published"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Assemble the review pack"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

    skills: [operations-review, trend-analysis]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, product-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/ops-review-minutes.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Pack incomplete → complete it": s1
  - id: d1
    decision: "Signals that need work?"
    owner: "Service owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Service owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Nothing new → send signals only": s4
  - id: s3
    do: "Raise problem records & backlog items"
    owner: "Problem manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-4-2-s3-raise-problem-records-and-backlog-items

    on:
      "Work competes with roadmap → product owner & sponsor": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Send the signal pack to EVOLVE"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

gate: "Operations review held"

  - "Postmortem actions reviewed"
checks:
  - "Pack completeness check"
on_failure:

  - "Signal pack is the meeting's required output"
rework: "Pack incomplete → complete it before the meeting"
outputs:
  - "docs/ops-review-minutes.md"
  - "docs/problem-record.md"
  - "docs/evolve-signal-pack.md"
handoff: "Operations signal pack → EVOLVE (Act VIII); problem records → 7.3.1; backlog items → PLAN"
learning:
  - "Decisions from the review that changed the roadmap — learning log"
```

# Workflow 7.2.1.1 · Declare an Incident

Check an alert or a report against the dashboard and the known errors, and declare and log an incident with one owner — or close the noise.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-2-1-1-declare

owner: "On-call engineer"

  - "docs/service-request.md"
  - "docs/known-error.md"
preconditions:
  - "Alerting live"
  - "On-call rota staffed"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Receive alert or report"
    owner: "On-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"

  - id: d1
    decision: "Real user impact?"
    owner: "On-call engineer"

    checkpoint: decision   # stop; On-call engineer decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "Unclear → gather more signals": s1
```

files.body:
# Workflow 7.2.3.1 · Restore the Service

Find the likely cause from telemetry and recent changes, apply the safest reversible mitigation, prove recovery on the SLIs and put affected data right.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-2-3-1-restore.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-2-3-1-run-restore`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-2-3-1-restore
title: "Restore the Service"
owner: "Operations lead"
inputs:
  - "docs/incident-record.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
  - "docs/deployment-record.md"
  - "docs/known-error.md"
preconditions:
  - "Commander named"
  - "Dashboard and runbook to hand"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Form hypotheses from telemetry & changes"
    owner: "Operations lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-3-1-s1-form-hypotheses-from-telemetry-and-changes
    skills: [change-correlation, kepner-tregoe-problem-analysis]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, vendor-reviewer, synthesiser, challenger]
    output: "docs/incident-timeline.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Apply the safest mitigation"
    owner: "On-call engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-3-1-s2-apply-the-safest-mitigation
    skills: [feature-flag-kill-switch, graceful-degradation, circuit-breaker]
    reviewers: [devops-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/incident-timeline.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Data repair, or no recovery in 30 min → service owner": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "SLIs recovered?"
    owner: "Incident commander"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Incident commander decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "No recovery → next hypothesis": s1
      "Cannot restore safely → controlled shutdown with comms": stop
  - id: s3
    do: "Put affected data right"
    owner: "Ops manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-3-1-s3-put-affected-data-right
    skills: [itil-4]
    reviewers: [domain-reviewer, data-reviewer]
    output: "docs/incident-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Resolve & request the hotfix"
    owner: "Incident commander"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-3-1-s4-resolve-and-request-the-hotfix
    skills: [change-enablement]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/hotfix-request.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Service Restored"
criteria:
  - "SLIs within SLO for 30 minutes"
  - "Every action timestamped"
checks:
  - "Second person on risky commands"
on_failure:
  - "Reverse the last action from the mitigation log"
  - "Hold resolution until SLIs are back for 30 minutes"
rework: "No recovery → next hypothesis"
outputs:
  - "docs/incident-timeline.md"
  - "docs/incident-record.md"
  - "docs/hotfix-request.md"
handoff: "Resolved incident record & timeline → 7.2.4 Run the Blameless Postmortem; hotfix request → BUILD (expedited iteration item)"
learning:
  - "Time to restore by mitigation type — learning log"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 7.2.4.1 · Write the Blameless Postmortem

Rebuild what happened from evidence, find the contributing factors in the system, agree owned actions and hand unresolved causes to problem management.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-2-4-1-postmortem.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-2-4-1-run-postmortem`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-2-4-1-postmortem
title: "Write the Blameless Postmortem"
owner: "Incident commander"
inputs:
  - "docs/incident-record.md"
  - "docs/incident-timeline.md"
preconditions:
  - "Incident resolved"
  - "Meets the postmortem threshold"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Reconstruct the timeline"
    owner: "Incident commander"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-4-1-s1-reconstruct-the-timeline
    skills: [timeline-reconstruction]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/incident-timeline.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Sev-3/4 → short review in the record": s4
  - id: s2
    do: "Analyse contributing factors"
    owner: "Responders"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-4-1-s2-analyse-contributing-factors
    skills: [fault-tree-analysis, five-whys, fishbone-diagram]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer, security-reviewer, reliability-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/postmortem.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Agree owned actions"
    owner: "Incident commander"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-4-1-s3-agree-owned-actions
    skills: [retrospective]
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer]
    output: "docs/postmortem-actions.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Actions unfunded → service owner": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "Blameless, evidenced, actions owned?"
    owner: "Service owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Service owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Blame or gaps → rewrite": s2
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish & raise problem records"
    owner: "Incident commander"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-2-4-1-s4-publish-and-raise-problem-records
    skills: [known-error-database]
    reviewers: [customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/problem-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Postmortem Accepted"
criteria:
  - "Timeline from evidence"
  - "Contributing factors, not one root cause"
  - "Actions owned and dated"
checks:
  - "Blameless-language review"
on_failure:
  - "Rewrite around decisions in context and the system that allowed them"
  - "Service owner assigns owners at the review"
rework: "Blame or gaps → rewrite the analysis"
outputs:
  - "docs/postmortem.md"
  - "docs/postmortem-actions.md"
  - "docs/problem-record.md"
handoff: "Postmortem & problem record → 7.3.1 Identify & Log Problems; actions → BUILD; learning → EVOLVE"
learning:
  - "Action completion rate at 30 days — learning log"
```

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-3-3-1-known-error

owner: "Problem manager"
inputs:
```

# Workflow 7.3.4.1 · Rank the Fix & Close the Problem

Put a price on the problem, rank its fix in the product backlog against features, and close it only when production shows it stopped.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-3-4-1-rank-and-close.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-3-4-1-run-rank-and-close`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-3-4-1-rank-and-close
title: "Rank the Fix & Close the Problem"
owner: "Problem manager"
inputs:
  - "docs/problem-record.md"
  - "docs/known-error.md"
  - "docs/product-backlog.md"
preconditions:
  - "Root cause confirmed"
  - "Known error published"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Cost the problem"
    owner: "Problem manager"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-3-4-1-s1-cost-the-problem
    skills: [cost-of-delay, trend-analysis]
    reviewers: [finance-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/problem-record.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Propose & estimate the fix"
    owner: "Engineering lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-3-4-1-s2-propose-and-estimate-the-fix
    skills: [backlog-refinement, scrum]
    reviewers: [engineering-reviewer]

    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s3
    do: "Rank against features"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-3-4-1-s3-rank-against-features
    skills: [wsjf, multi-level-backlog]
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, business-reviewer]
    output: "docs/product-backlog.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: d1
    decision: "Fix now?"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Product owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Rank disputed → sponsor": authority

  - id: s4

  - "Cost in €/month"

  - "Recurrence check"
on_failure:

outputs:
  - "docs/product-backlog.md"
  - "docs/fix-verification.md"
handoff: "Problem fix as a product backlog entry → PLAN (ranking) and BUILD; fix verification → EVOLVE"
learning:
  - "Time from problem logged to fix verified — learning log"
```

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-4-3-1-triage
title: "Answer or Route a Contact"
owner: "Service desk agent"

preconditions:

steps:
```

```yaml
preconditions:
  - "SBOM current for the running release"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Match findings to the SBOM"
    owner: "Security analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
```

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-6-3-response.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-6-3-run-response`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
orchestration: operate-7-6-3-response
title: "Respond to Security Incidents"
owner: "Security analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/security-event.md"
  - "docs/detection-catalogue.md"
  - "docs/runbook.md"
entry:
  - "Security alert raised"
runs:
  - unit: "7.6.3.1 Contain a Security Incident"
    spec: workflows/operate-7-6-3-1-contain.md
    command: operate-7-6-3-1-run-contain
    gate: "Threat Contained"
    checkpoint: review   # show outputs, wait for go-ahead
parallel:
  - "Containment ∥ evidence preservation ∥ notification assessment"
gate: "Threat Contained"
decided_by: "The security lead directs containment; the DPO decides notification; the service owner decides on shutdown."
criteria:
  - "Contained within 1 hour of confirmation for high severity"
  - "Evidence preserved before changes"
routes:
  forward: "Security postmortem → Problem Management; fixes → BUILD; posture → EVOLVE"
  rework: "Re-infection → contain again"
  alternate: "False positive → tune the detection"
  escalate: "Personal-data breach → DPO and legal (72 h)"

  - "docs/breach-notification.md"
```

files.body:
# Workflow 7.6.4.1 · Recertify Access & Report Posture

Have every account's owner justify its access, revoke what isn't justified, rotate secrets and report the posture with evidence.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-6-4-1-access-review.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-6-4-1-run-access-review`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-6-4-1-access-review
title: "Recertify Access & Report Posture"
owner: "Security analyst"
inputs:
  - "docs/access-review.md"
  - "docs/vulnerability-register.md"
preconditions:
  - "Quarter end or a leaver / role change"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Export accounts & privileges"
    owner: "Security analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-6-4-1-s1-export-accounts-and-privileges
    reviewers: [security-reviewer]
    output: "docs/access-review.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s2
    do: "Owners recertify"
    owner: "Account owners"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-6-4-1-s2-owners-recertify
    skills: [access-recertification, single-accountable-owner]
    reviewers: [governance-reviewer, vendor-reviewer]
    output: "docs/access-review.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
    on:
      "Owner unresponsive → security lead suspends": authority
  - id: d1
    decision: "Every access justified?"
    owner: "Security lead"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Security lead decides
    branches:
      "yes": s3
      "All justified → report": s4
      "Rubber-stamped sample → recertify again": s2
  - id: s3
    do: "Revoke & rotate secrets"
    owner: "Platform engineer"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-6-4-1-s3-revoke-and-rotate-secrets
    skills: [secrets-rotation]
    reviewers: [privacy-reviewer]
    output: "docs/access-review.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
  - id: s4
    do: "Report posture with evidence"
    owner: "Security analyst"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-6-4-1-s4-report-posture-with-evidence
    skills: [nist-cybersecurity-framework]
    reviewers: [compliance-reviewer, synthesiser]
    output: "docs/posture-report.md"
    checkpoint: review-at-end
gate: "Posture Review"
criteria:
  - "Owner and reason per account"
  - "Secrets ≤ 90 days"
checks:
  - "10% sample"
on_failure:
  - "Sample 10% and reject the batch on failure"
  - "Vault enforces rotation expiry"
rework: "Rubber-stamped sample → recertify again"
outputs:
  - "docs/access-review.md"
  - "docs/posture-report.md"
handoff: "Security posture report → EVOLVE and compliance"
learning:
  - "Access found unjustified and how it arose — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VII OPERATE · Scale: Product team. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
OPERATE is part of the **Run & learn** — Is it working, and what did we learn? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## OPERATE: Run the service reliably, securely and economically; respond to failure; and turn what running it teaches into signals the next cycle can act on.
- **7.1 Observability & Monitoring** — gate: SLO & Error Budget. Produces: SLO specification, Error-budget policy, Service dashboard, Alert rules, On-call rota, Error-budget report, Release freeze notice, Operations signal digest, Operations signal pack.
- **7.2 Incident Management** — gate: Service Restored. Produces: Incident record, Incident status update, Incident timeline, Hotfix request, Postmortem, Problem record.
- **7.3 Problem Management** — gate: Problem Review. Produces: Problem record, Problem investigation, Known-error record, Knowledge-base article, Product backlog entry, Fix verification.
- **7.4 Service Request & Support** — gate: Support Service Review. Produces: Service catalogue, Support model, Service request, Feedback record, Knowledge-base article, Support report.
- **7.5 Capacity & Cost** — gate: Capacity & Cost Review. Produces: Demand forecast, Capacity plan, Load-test results, Cost-to-serve report, Optimisation log.
- **7.6 Security Operations** — gate: Security Posture Review. Produces: Vulnerability register, Detection rule catalogue, Security event record, Breach notification, Access review, Security posture report, Hotfix request.
- Act gate: **SLO & Error Budget** — decided by: Service owner applies the error-budget policy and lifts freezes; incident commander directs incidents; product owner ranks problem fixes; DPO decides breach notification..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: SLO → ALR → INC → PM → PRB → KE → SR → CAP → VUL → EBR → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `operate-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Product team
Write for a product trio and a delivery team. Use our shared templates, make outputs ready to drop into the backlog or repository, and flag anything that needs the team's refinement.
Access: Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.

# Guardrails & hooks — Operate

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Product team
- Read and write the shared workspace and backlog; agents propose changes, people merge and publish.
- Watch for: Each person's agent producing inconsistent artifacts — use the shared templates
- Watch for: Discovery and delivery drifting apart

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### OPERATE
- Budget spent → only reliability fixes and security patches release
- No silent fixes of user-visible failures
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect
- Whoever records readings does not judge them
- On-call is staffed, rested and paid
- Postmortems are blameless
- Production data used for analysis only anonymised
- Error budgets
- On-call capacity
- Vendor limits and quotas
- Legal notification deadlines

### 7.1 Observability & Monitoring
- No SLO at 100%
- Budget spent → only reliability fixes and security patches release
- SLOs reviewed quarterly
- On-call load ≤ 2 pages per shift on average
- Telemetry cost
- No personal data in logs

### 7.1.1 Define SLIs & SLOs
- An SLO without an error-budget policy is not agreed
- Never set an SLO at 100%
- SLOs reviewed at least quarterly
- Any external SLA looser than the internal SLO
- What can be measured today

### 7.1.2 Instrument & Build Dashboards
- No personal data or order contents in logs, labels or traces
- OpenTelemetry naming conventions
- Log retention follows the data policy
- Telemetry cost
- No personal data in logs

### 7.1.3 Alert on SLO Burn
- Every page is actionable
- No alert without an owner
- On-call load: at most 2 pages per shift on average
- On-call is paid and rested per policy
- On-call capacity

### 7.1.4 Track the Error Budget
- Budget spent → only reliability fixes and security patches release
- Whoever recorded the readings does not judge them
- Freeze lifted only by the service owner
- Report monthly and at every gate decision
- Policy agreed in advance, not during the argument

### 7.2 Incident Management
- One commander at a time
- Reversible mitigations first
- No names as causes
- Update cadence by severity
- Postmortem within 5 working days for Sev-1/2
- Update cadence
- Reversible actions first

### 7.2.1 Detect & Log
- When in doubt, declare — downgrading is cheap
- No silent fixes of user-visible failures
- All incidents logged in the service desk tool
- Clerk reports count as detection signals
- Paging policy

### 7.2.2 Classify & Command
- The commander coordinates and does not debug
- Hand-overs of command are announced
- Updates every 30 min for Sev-1/2 and every 2 h for Sev-3
- Customer notices approved by the communications lead
- Update cadence

### 7.2.3 Mitigate & Restore
- Prefer reversible mitigations: flag off, roll back, fail over
- No data repair without the commander's approval
- Hotfixes still pass the pipeline and the DoD essentials
- Affected customers' data put right before close
- Reversible actions first

### 7.2.4 Run the Blameless Postmortem
- No names as causes; describe decisions in their context
- Unresolved causes become problem records
- Postmortem within 5 working days for Sev-1/2
- Actions reviewed at the operations review
- 5-day deadline

### 7.3 Problem Management
- One backlog, one order — no side queue for fixes
- Every known error links to its problem
- Problems reviewed monthly at the operations review
- Accepted problems reviewed quarterly
- Investigation timebox
- Sprint capacity

### 7.3.1 Identify & Log Problems
- One problem record per cause
- Problems reviewed monthly at the operations review
- Problem manager capacity

### 7.3.2 Investigate Root Cause
- Evidence before conclusions
- Investigation timeboxed (10 working days by default)
- Production data used only anonymised
- Investigation timebox

### 7.3.3 Record Known Errors & Workarounds
- Every known error links to its problem record
- Retired when the fix is verified
- Known errors searchable from the service desk tool
- Clerk time

### 7.3.4 Rank & Resolve in the Backlog
- One backlog, one order — no side queue for fixes
- Close only on evidence of no recurrence
- Problem items ranked with WSJF like features
- Accepted problems reviewed quarterly
- Sprint capacity

### 7.4 Service Request & Support
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect
- Every contact gets a reply saying what happens next
- First-contact resolution tracked
- SLAs reviewed quarterly
- Support staffing
- Response SLAs

### 7.4.1 Run the Path to Help
- No help through personal inboxes
- Intake meets WCAG 2.2 AA
- SLAs reviewed quarterly against the support report
- Support staffing

### 7.4.2 Fulfil Service Requests
- Access requests follow least privilege
- Standard requests need no extra approval
- Every request logged, even if solved on the phone
- SLA

### 7.4.3 Triage Questions & Feedback
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect
- Every contact gets a reply saying what happens next
- First-contact resolution tracked
- Feedback records reviewed weekly by the product owner
- Response SLA

### 7.4.4 Maintain the Knowledge Base
- No personal data or secrets in articles
- Articles reviewed every 6 months and when their fix ships
- Article reuse counted
- Reviewer time

### 7.5 Capacity & Cost
- Changes go through change enablement
- No optimisation while the error budget is spent
- Capacity reviewed before each peak and site rollout
- Cost reviewed monthly with finance
- Budget
- Vendor quotas

### 7.5.1 Forecast Demand

- Length of data history

### 7.5.2 Plan & Test Capacity
- Changes go through change enablement
- No load testing against the production ERP
- Plan reviewed before each site rollout and each peak
- Budget
- Vendor quotas

### 7.5.3 Measure Cost to Serve

- Monthly report; quarterly review with finance
- Budget

### 7.5.4 Right-size & Optimise
- No optimisation while the error budget is spent
- Clerk time counts as cost
- Optimisation log reviewed monthly
- Error budget

### 7.6 Security Operations
- Least privilege
- Evidence preserved before containment changes
- Personal-data breaches assessed within 72 hours
- Exceptions time-limited and owned

- 72-hour notification clock
- Patch windows

### 7.6.1 Manage Vulnerabilities

- Base images rebuilt weekly
- SBOM kept current per release
- Patch windows
- Error budget for redeploys

- Security logs kept 12 months
- Log costs
- Personal data in logs

- Chain of custody for evidence

- Restricted distribution of details
- 72-hour clock

# Workflow 7.1.1.1 · Set SLOs & the Budget Policy

Turn the journeys users depend on into SLIs, set targets from real baselines and agree what happens when the budget runs out.

**Run it:** ask your agent to "run `workflows/operate-7-1-1-1-set-slos.md` for {{initiative}}, stopping at every checkpoint", or use the command `operate-7-1-1-1-run-set-slos`. Each checkpoint means: show me the output and wait. At `decision` checkpoints the named person decides.

```yaml
workflow: operate-7-1-1-1-set-slos
title: "Set SLOs & the Budget Policy"
owner: "Product owner"
inputs:
  - "docs/release-record.md"
  - "docs/ops-pdv.md"
  - "docs/ops-slo-targets.md"
preconditions:
  - "Service live in at least one site"
  - "28 days of data, or the SLO marked provisional"
steps:
  - id: s1
    do: "Map critical user journeys"
    owner: "Product owner"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s1-map-critical-user-journeys
    reviewers: [product-reviewer, customer-reviewer]
    output: "docs/critical-journeys.md"
    checkpoint: review
    on:
      "Journey not worth an SLO → monitor only": stop
  - id: s2
    do: "Choose SLIs per journey"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s2-choose-slis-per-journey
    skills: [site-reliability-engineering, golden-signals, red-method]
    reviewers: [reliability-reviewer, ai-reviewer]
    output: "docs/slo-spec.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: s3
    do: "Set targets from baselines"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s3-set-targets-from-baselines
    skills: [burn-rate-calculation]
    reviewers: [performance-reviewer, operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/slo-spec.md"
    checkpoint: review
  - id: d1
    decision: "Owners agree targets & budget policy?"
    owner: "Service owner"
    agent: "prepare a decision brief — never decide"
    checkpoint: decision   # stop; Service owner decides
    branches:
      "yes": s4
      "Target disputed → re-derive from baseline": s3
      "Owners deadlocked → sponsor": authority
  - id: s4
    do: "Publish SLOs & policy"
    owner: "SRE lead"
    agent: "draft, then wait for review"
    command: operate-7-1-1-1-s4-publish-slos-and-policy
    skills: [error-budget]
    reviewers: [operations-reviewer]
    output: "docs/error-budget-policy.md"
    checkpoint: review
gate: "SLO Agreement"
criteria:
  - "Good / valid ratio, target, window and owner for every SLO"
checks:
  - "Baseline check"
  - "Product owner reads each SLO as user impact"
on_failure:
  - "Re-derive the SLI from user-facing events"
  - "Set a provisional SLO with a review date"
rework: "Disputed target → re-derive from the baseline"
outputs:
  - "docs/critical-journeys.md"
  - "docs/slo-spec.md"
  - "docs/error-budget-policy.md"
handoff: "SLO specification & error-budget policy → 7.1.2 Instrument & Build Dashboards"
learning:
  - "SLOs revised in their first quarter, and why — learning log"
```

# AGENTS.md — {{initiative}}

> Node SDLC · Act VII OPERATE · Scale: Enterprise. Read this first, every session.

## How we work
People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.
- **You:** Choose what to work on · give context · make decisions · review and correct · sign off · own the artifact
- **Your agent:** Draft · research · summarise · structure into templates · spot gaps and risks · check against criteria · prepare options

## Where this act sits
OPERATE is part of the **Run & learn** — Is it working, and what did we learn? The acts keep their order as a logical dependency — a problem is validated before it is planned, designed before it is built — but they are kinds of work that run continuously and in parallel, at different sizes, not phases on a calendar.

## OPERATE: Run the service reliably, securely and economically; respond to failure; and turn what running it teaches into signals the next cycle can act on.
- **7.1 Observability & Monitoring** — gate: SLO & Error Budget. Produces: SLO specification, Error-budget policy, Service dashboard, Alert rules, On-call rota, Error-budget report, Release freeze notice, Operations signal digest, Operations signal pack.
- **7.2 Incident Management** — gate: Service Restored. Produces: Incident record, Incident status update, Incident timeline, Hotfix request, Postmortem, Problem record.
- **7.3 Problem Management** — gate: Problem Review. Produces: Problem record, Problem investigation, Known-error record, Knowledge-base article, Product backlog entry, Fix verification.
- **7.4 Service Request & Support** — gate: Support Service Review. Produces: Service catalogue, Support model, Service request, Feedback record, Knowledge-base article, Support report.
- **7.5 Capacity & Cost** — gate: Capacity & Cost Review. Produces: Demand forecast, Capacity plan, Load-test results, Cost-to-serve report, Optimisation log.
- **7.6 Security Operations** — gate: Security Posture Review. Produces: Vulnerability register, Detection rule catalogue, Security event record, Breach notification, Access review, Security posture report, Hotfix request.
- Act gate: **SLO & Error Budget** — decided by: Service owner applies the error-budget policy and lifts freezes; incident commander directs incidents; product owner ranks problem fixes; DPO decides breach notification..

## Conventions
- Artifacts live in `docs/<artifact>.md`, written from `templates/<artifact>.md`.
- Every artifact carries its trace ID and links the IDs upstream of it; register new IDs in `TRACE.md`.
- Trace chain: SLO → ALR → INC → PM → PRB → KE → SR → CAP → VUL → EBR → LRN.
- Log each step in `PROGRESS.md`.
- Before saving, score the artifact against `rubrics/<artifact>.md`.

## Your toolkit
- `commands/` — one per step, workflow, subprocess, process and the act. Start with `operate-run-act` or the unit you're on.
- `workflows/` — run specs with checkpoints; stop at every checkpoint.
- `skills/` — how-to packages for each technique; load the ones a command names.
- `agents/` — reviewers by lens, plus researcher, synthesiser, challenger and decision-brief writer.
- `TOOLS.md` and `GUARDRAILS.md` — what you may use and must never do.

## Ground rules
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.

## Scale: Enterprise
Use formal language and our approved templates. Back every claim with a reference to its evidence for audit, flag compliance, security and privacy implications, name the approver for each decision, and keep confidential details out of anything meant for wider sharing.
Access: Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.

# Guardrails & hooks — Operate

People own the work, agents help do it. In every unit the person in the role briefs the agent, gives it the right context, checks what it produces, and makes every decision. The agent drafts, researches, analyses, structures and checks — it never decides, approves or signs.

## Always
- Don't invent facts, figures, quotes or sources — mark anything unverified as an assumption.
- If something you need is missing, ask me instead of guessing.
- Keep personal or confidential data out unless I've provided it for this purpose.
- Prepare decisions; don't make them — I decide.
- Never paste passwords, keys, or personal data you aren't allowed to share — anonymise first
- At enterprise scale, use only approved tools
- Check every fact, number and source the agent gives you
- Agents prepare decisions; people make them
- Save the output in the artifact template and note that an agent helped
- If the agent's output is wrong, correct the prompt or the context — then record what you learned

## Scale: Enterprise
- Approved tools only; read-only on customer and production data; every write goes through review; agent actions logged for audit.
- Watch for: Pasting confidential or personal data into unapproved tools
- Watch for: Agent output in audited artifacts without a human reviewer named

## Hooks — automatic where your agent supports them, a checklist everywhere else
| When | Check | If it fails |
|---|---|---|
| Before saving an artifact | It follows its template · it carries its trace ID and links upstream IDs · every claim cites evidence or is marked 'Assumption:' · no personal data or secrets | Fix, or stop and tell me |
| Before a decision step | Stop. Prepare the decision brief. Wait for the named decision-maker | Never decide or approve |
| Before anything leaves the team | Messages, posts, invitations and shared documents are drafts until a person sends them | Ask for approval |
| Before using a new tool or data source | Is it allowed at this scale? Is the data allowed in this tool? | Ask first |
| After each step | Append to PROGRESS.md: date, unit, what was done, artifacts, decisions, open questions, next | Always |

## Rules and policies by unit
### OPERATE
- Budget spent → only reliability fixes and security patches release
- No silent fixes of user-visible failures
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect
- Whoever records readings does not judge them
- On-call is staffed, rested and paid
- Postmortems are blameless
- Production data used for analysis only anonymised
- Error budgets
- On-call capacity
- Vendor limits and quotas
- Legal notification deadlines

### 7.1 Observability & Monitoring
- No SLO at 100%
- Budget spent → only reliability fixes and security patches release
- SLOs reviewed quarterly
- On-call load ≤ 2 pages per shift on average
- Telemetry cost
- No personal data in logs

### 7.1.1 Define SLIs & SLOs
- An SLO without an error-budget policy is not agreed
- Never set an SLO at 100%
- SLOs reviewed at least quarterly
- Any external SLA looser than the internal SLO
- What can be measured today

### 7.1.2 Instrument & Build Dashboards
- No personal data or order contents in logs, labels or traces
- OpenTelemetry naming conventions
- Log retention follows the data policy
- Telemetry cost
- No personal data in logs

### 7.1.3 Alert on SLO Burn
- Every page is actionable
- No alert without an owner
- On-call load: at most 2 pages per shift on average
- On-call is paid and rested per policy
- On-call capacity

### 7.1.4 Track the Error Budget
- Budget spent → only reliability fixes and security patches release
- Whoever recorded the readings does not judge them
- Freeze lifted only by the service owner
- Report monthly and at every gate decision
- Policy agreed in advance, not during the argument

### 7.2 Incident Management
- One commander at a time
- Reversible mitigations first
- No names as causes
- Update cadence by severity
- Postmortem within 5 working days for Sev-1/2
- Update cadence
- Reversible actions first

### 7.2.1 Detect & Log
- When in doubt, declare — downgrading is cheap
- No silent fixes of user-visible failures
- All incidents logged in the service desk tool
- Clerk reports count as detection signals
- Paging policy

### 7.2.2 Classify & Command
- The commander coordinates and does not debug
- Hand-overs of command are announced
- Updates every 30 min for Sev-1/2 and every 2 h for Sev-3
- Customer notices approved by the communications lead
- Update cadence

### 7.2.3 Mitigate & Restore
- Prefer reversible mitigations: flag off, roll back, fail over
- No data repair without the commander's approval
- Hotfixes still pass the pipeline and the DoD essentials
- Affected customers' data put right before close
- Reversible actions first

### 7.2.4 Run the Blameless Postmortem
- No names as causes; describe decisions in their context
- Unresolved causes become problem records
- Postmortem within 5 working days for Sev-1/2
- Actions reviewed at the operations review
- 5-day deadline

### 7.3 Problem Management
- One backlog, one order — no side queue for fixes
- Every known error links to its problem
- Problems reviewed monthly at the operations review
- Accepted problems reviewed quarterly
- Investigation timebox
- Sprint capacity

### 7.3.1 Identify & Log Problems
- One problem record per cause
- Problems reviewed monthly at the operations review
- Problem manager capacity

### 7.3.2 Investigate Root Cause
- Evidence before conclusions
- Investigation timeboxed (10 working days by default)
- Production data used only anonymised
- Investigation timebox

### 7.3.3 Record Known Errors & Workarounds
- Every known error links to its problem record
- Retired when the fix is verified
- Known errors searchable from the service desk tool
- Clerk time

### 7.3.4 Rank & Resolve in the Backlog
- One backlog, one order — no side queue for fixes
- Close only on evidence of no recurrence
- Problem items ranked with WSJF like features
- Accepted problems reviewed quarterly
- Sprint capacity

### 7.4 Service Request & Support
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect
- Every contact gets a reply saying what happens next
- First-contact resolution tracked
- SLAs reviewed quarterly
- Support staffing
- Response SLAs

### 7.4.1 Run the Path to Help
- No help through personal inboxes
- Intake meets WCAG 2.2 AA
- SLAs reviewed quarterly against the support report
- Support staffing

### 7.4.2 Fulfil Service Requests
- Access requests follow least privilege

- Every request logged, even if solved on the phone

### 7.4.3 Triage Questions & Feedback
- A metric below target is a signal, not a defect
- Every contact gets a reply saying what happens next
- First-contact resolution tracked
- Feedback records reviewed weekly by the product owner
- Response SLA

### 7.4.4 Maintain the Knowledge Base
- No personal data or secrets in articles
- Articles reviewed every 6 months and when their fix ships
- Article reuse counted
- Reviewer time

### 7.5 Capacity & Cost
- Changes go through change enablement
- No optimisation while the error budget is spent
- Capacity reviewed before each peak and site rollout
- Cost reviewed monthly with finance
- Budget
- Vendor quotas

### 7.5.1 Forecast Demand

### 7.5.2 Plan & Test Capacity
- Changes go through change enablement
- No load testing against the production ERP

- Budget
- Vendor quotas

### 7.5.3 Measure Cost to Serve

- Budget

### 7.5.4 Right-size & Optimise
- No optimisation while the error budget is spent
- Clerk time counts as cost
- Optimisation log reviewed monthly
- Error budget

### 7.6 Security Operations
- Least privilege
- Evidence preserved before containment changes
- Personal-data breaches assessed within 72 hours
- Exceptions time-limited and owned
- Security logs kept 12 months
- 72-hour notification clock
- Patch windows

### 7.6.1 Manage Vulnerabilities
- Every exception time-limited and owned

- Patch windows

### 7.6.2 Monitor Security Events

### 7.6.3 Respond to Security Incidents
- Personal-data breaches assessed for notification within 72 hours
- Chain of custody for evidence

- 72-hour clock

- No shared personal accounts

- Evidence kept 3 years for audit
- Audit timetable
